findings: Prompt filter: Pavo refuses any prompt containing the KJV word 'naked' (text_rejected_porn) - Genesis 3:7, 3:10, 3:11 cannot be spoken by Pavo verbatim. The adapter reports this as status 'incomplete' (submission 'unknown'); the block is only visible in the conversation history. It is not the E124 quota signal.

Exact words: every generated speech clip says the KJV/narration words exactly (WER 0.0 on base.en, small.en and medium.en without timestamps; 5 of 5 clips, plus B). base.en and small.en hear 'gavest' as 'gave us' (WER 0.105) on Pavo AND on our own Kokoro rendition; medium.en hears 'gavest' on both: an ASR limit, not Pavo. The QA's base.en would score that line 0.105 (> 0.1) for Kokoro too.

Diction: mean word probability 0.88-0.98; low-confidence words are sentence-initial function words only ('Where', 'this', 'Because'); the archaic words actually spoken (art, thou, hast, gavest) were recognised (gavest by medium.en). thy/thee/wast were only in the two blocked lines, and no generated line names Eden/Adam/Eve, so their pronunciation is untested. No mispronounced word found by any model.
Music: none. YAMNet music share 0.0 on 6 of 7 clips, 0.04 (one frame) on s-c4-point; the positive 'only the voice and natural ambient sound' wording worked.
Ambience: inconsistent. Talking/narration clips are almost dry (gaps near -100 dBFS), God's clip has full-band wind, the silent clip has birds at -43 LUFS: at a cut the room tone jumps.

Voice consistency: one voice for the Keeper across clips (0.932). Adam is self-consistent within a scene (0.957) and fairly across scenes (0.88-0.89), but not distinct from the narrator (0.85-0.89 vs 0.52-0.56 for our Kokoro pair): a viewer may hear Adam and the Keeper as the same man.

Loudness per clip varies 13 LU among speech clips (-14.7 to -27.6 LUFS integrated; God -27.6). Concat (a), raw: -16.5 LUFS, LRA 12.8, TP -1.0 (outside -16..-14, TP at the -1 limit). Concat (b), static per-clip voice gain + 80 ms crossfades + continuous wind bed + owned music ducked + loudnorm: -15.0 LUFS, LRA 5.9, TP -1.4 (inside the band).

Lip sync with Pavo's own audio: both Adam talking clips pass the SyncNet gate with margin (conf 8.08, 6.61, 7.33 vs min 2.7; offset -2 in -3..0). Voice-over clips: no MOUTH_TALKING (the on-screen face does not mouth the narration), but MOUTH_NOT_CLOSED (lips parted, as in 'afraid/stunned'); God's clip: no face.

Timing: the first word starts at 0.0 s in 2 clips and speech ends 0.1-0.5 s before the clip end; no breath before or after (prompt B's 'short breath before' did not help: B starts at 0.68 s, A at 1.16 s). Pace 1.9-3.0 words/s.
Picture: golden glyph-like streaks on Eve's hair in both Adam-and-Eve two-shots (s-c2-adam, s-c4-blame, contact.jpg at 12 s and 46-50 s); clip_check finds no flag, Claude's vetting would.

verdict: Not yet at 9.5 as a whole, but closer than expected. Exact KJV words, clear archaic diction, no music and lip sync all pass with the structured prompt A. Blockers: (1) Pavo's filter refuses lines with 'naked' - those lines need another source (our Kokoro + Pavo audio-input binding); (2) Adam's voice is not distinct from the Keeper's - a character-voice identity cannot be pinned by words alone; (3) ambience and level differ per clip and need the mix-b treatment; (4) the two-shot glyph artifacts. A hybrid is the realistic path: Pavo native speech for the Keeper and for lines that pass the filter, measured per clip (WER with medium.en, SyncNet, speaker cosine against an anchor clip of that character), with a fallback to our Kokoro voice for refused lines - which reintroduces two voices for one character unless the anchor is chosen from Pavo.
